The heat input to the HTF was assumed constant over the entire HTF flow length for that flow pass; however, the heat transfer rate differs between flow passes (represented by different simulated tubes within the 2D CFD). Computed fluid temperature at the center point of each flow pass (in 2D CFD model) was used to set the wall boundary condition for the next time step. Convective boundary condition at tube walls was updated at every time step using the computed HTF temperature T, and HTF f heat transfer coefficient from Gnielinski correlation [40] evaluated at local conditions.
